about: Settilio, Permesso for seven (Torino 1787, «Del giuoco di Permesso in sette persone, o sia Settilio», p. 77, and the Fool of pp. 77-78), «giuoco bizzarro»: 11 cards to each of the seven players and one card over «per lo scarto»; the rest is said to be as in Quintilio and Sestilio. The book does not say who takes the card over; ours, as the dealer, who then puts one card away. Giuoco sciolto is inherited from Sestilio because «come sopra è stato detto di Quintilio, e Sestilio» (p. 77); that it applies with seven is our reading, and so is the card over: in the free game too it is the dealer's and he puts one card away, since 7 × 11 leaves one (the book's «no discard» of p. 77 is said of six).

dummett1980.cite: Michael Dummett, The Game of Tarot, London: Duckworth, 1980, chapter XIII «Tarocco in Piedmont and Lombardy», pp. 258-279 (our scan is partial: printed page 268 is missing)

count.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 77: «Del giuoco di Permesso in sette persone, o sia Settilio».

mode.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 77: «Il rimanente si farà come sopra è stato detto di Quintilio, e Sestilio»: one against the rest.

deck.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 77: 7 × 11 + 1 = 78 («undici carte per ciascun giuocatore, sicchè una carta sola resterà per lo scarto»); the sum is not printed.

contracts.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 60, 67: «Permesso» asks to call three cards and put three away; «Chi va a tre carte, guadagna l'Onoranza di due».
[D] Torino 1787, pp. 62, 67: «A due»; «chi va a due carte guadagna l'Onoranza di tre».
[D] Torino 1787, pp. 63, 67: «io vado ad una»; «chi va a una carta sola, guadagna l'Onoranza di quattro».
[D] Torino 1787, pp. 64, 67: «aller sans prendre», no card changed; «chi va a sans prendre, guadagna l'Onoranza di cinque».

[R] Torino 1787, pp. 76-77: «giuoco sciolto, in cui chi fa più punti guadagna la partita»; rules of the Dottore, without discard. Said for six (p. 76). For seven the page says only «Il rimanente si farà come sopra è stato detto di Quintilio, e Sestilio» (p. 77): carried over to Settilio, our reading.

variants.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 76: «potrassi giuocare a giuoco sciolto, in cui chi fa più punti guadagna la partita»: the table agrees before the deal to play giuoco sciolto instead of Permesso, with no auction: nobody asks «Permesso», the cards are dealt and play begins at once, each for himself. For seven the page says only «Il rimanente si farà come sopra è stato detto di Quintilio, e Sestilio» (p. 77): carried over to Settilio, our reading; the one card over (p. 77, «per lo scarto») is still put away by the dealer.

contracts.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 76: only giuoco sciolto is played; nobody asks «Permesso», so there is no auction. Said for six; carried over to seven (p. 77).

all_pass.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 76: the table plays «a giuoco sciolto» as agreed. Said for six; carried over to seven (p. 77).

variants.source: [R] Dummett 1980, p. 267 (not printed in the Turin book): if all six pass, the cards are not thrown in but «giuoco sciolto» is played; the book itself (p. 76) offers it as a choice, not as the end of a general pass.

all_pass.source: [R] Dummett 1980, p. 267: a general pass leads to giuoco sciolto; the book says only that it may be played (p. 76).

tie.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 70: «tu non guadagni, nè perdi: la partita … a mischiare, e dar i Tarocchi». [S] The drawn hand counts as a dealt hand in the round of dealers (match.dealer_rounds): nobody pays and the next player deals; ours.

bands.source: [R] Torino 1787, pp. 66-70: 46 and more wins (p. 68); «quarantatrè punti e mezzo, ovvero quarantaquattro, … o quarantacinque» loses «solo dell'Onoranza» (pp. 66-67); «quarantacinque, e mezzo, ovvero quarantacinque, e non abbi avuto il Folle» is a draw (p. 70). The book does not contradict itself: the numbers are named before the card for the Fool changes hands (p. 68: «quarantasei punti, e a te non devo dare la carta del Folle»), and that card is worth half a point. After it is paid, 45½ is a draw, 46 and more win and 45 and less lose: the lone player who made 45 and is owed the card ends at 45½ (a draw), with 45 and no card owed he loses the Onoranza only. count.fool_card counts the points after the card is paid. [R] The line between the Onoranza alone and the full loss is drawn where the payment puts it: 43 is no step below 45 (settle.amount rounds 43 to 45), so 43 to 45 lose the Onoranza alone and 42½ or less lose in full; pp. 66-67 name 43½, 44, 44½ and 45. The money is the same as with the line at 43½; only the name of the band at 43 changes. Other reading (alt): the numbers of pp. 66-70 are the final count and 45 is a draw too.

overbid_returns.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 62 (Permesso for three; p. 77 sends to it, «come sopra è stato detto di Quintilio, e Sestilio»): the second reading of «dirà subito», carried over to seven: the word returns at once to the seat that was overbid, who holds with an equal bid, overbids or gives way. Said of three players; the transfer is ours. Torino [1846], part I, p. 42 (where the word goes round: the reading played) and Dummett 1980, p. 265 (the pair scheme of the other reading) are named at Permesso for three; the pages for this number of players have no example of their own.

replace.what: who has the word after a raise in the auction

hand_size.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 77: «undici carte per ciascun giuocatore».

dealer_extra.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 77: «una carta sola resterà per lo scarto»: one card is over and is the discard; who takes it is not said. Ours: the dealer (Dummett 1980, p. 267: he takes the last card and puts one away).

dead.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 77: 7 × 11 + 1 = 78; nothing is left over (the sum is not printed).

phases.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 77: «una carta sola resterà per lo scarto».

who.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 77 does not say who takes the card over. Ours, after Dummett 1980, p. 267: the dealer «takes the last card for himself, discarding one».

count.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 77: «una carta sola resterà per lo scarto»: one card is put away.

count_mode.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 77: one card put away; exactly one, as the hand must have 11 cards for the tricks.

discard_honours_barred.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 34 (general rule 38): «cioè nessun Re, nè l'Angelo, nè il Folle, nè Bagatto si potrà scartare»; the Permesso sections (pp. 59-60) do not repeat it, so the general rule is carried over. Other reading: the Permesso discard is free.

allowed_exceptions.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 34 (rule 38): «eccetto che Bagatto sia solo, senza il Folle»: «solo» is read as the only trump of the hand, as Dummett 1980, p. 259 reads this rule («neither the Folle nor any other trump»). Revision 1 read it as «holding no Fool». The exception for the Fool «in un sol caso … vola» is not played (see left_out). Other reading: no exception, as the rules of 1830 have it (Dummett, p. 259).

counts_for.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 21, rule 10 (for every game), lists among the things to be agreed before the deal whether a player «avendo o il Folle, o lo scarto» loses the «vola»: it supposes that a player with no trick may keep his discard, and no Turin book prints the contrary for a game with one discard. Pages 59-60 (Permesso for three) and p. 77 (seven, one card left for the discard) do not say whose points the discard joins; ours: the side of the player who put it away, the dealer. Other reading: a side with no trick gives the discard to the taker of the last trick. That a player with no trick loses his discard is printed only in Prammatica [1846], pp. 24-25, n. 15 «Mittigati in due collo scarto compito», a game for two: «La così detta vola … perde i punti dei due scarti, tanto piccolo che grande», and the Fool with them («e con essi anche il Folle»); the page does not say who gains them. Dummett 1980, p. 259 gives a rule for it («they must surrender the discarded cards to the player or side winning the last trick») and names no source. See OPEN_QUESTIONS.md, question 1.

replace.what: the discard of a player who won no trick: kept or lost

announce.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 60: «distintamente, e chiaramente ho scartato: … più non potrai cambiar alcuna carta».

left_out.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 100: «Vola, dicesi del fare tutte le basi»; the stake of a vola is agreed before the deal (p. 21 rule 10).
left_out.why: The book gives no figure and no rule of a vola inside Permesso; a premium of the table, not played.

left_out.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 66, 99: the game may be played «unicamente a guadagnar la partita col marcio»; «Marcio, vale posta doppia … facendo o … a cui la partita è fissata».
left_out.why: Two ways of playing (in coins or only for the game with marcio) are named but the book gives neither a line for the marcio at Permesso nor its payment; only the coin game is played.

left_out.source: [S] Torino 1787, p. 70 prints only «tu non guadagni, nè perdi» for a drawn hand; it says nothing of the stakes on the table.
left_out.why: A drawn hand pays nothing in the ledger.

effect.source: [R] Torino 1787, pp. 59-60 (Permesso for three): a card more or fewer in the discard: «si faran tutti, quantunque abbi guadagnato, da … semplice, se la faran pagar doppia»; carried over to the one card the dealer puts away at Settilio (p. 77); the engine checks the count.
[R] Torino 1787, p. 60: «fatto lo scarto, e detto, ho scartato, più non potrai cambiar alcuna carta»; carried over to Settilio (p. 77).
[D] Torino 1787, pp. 64-65: «pagherà la partita semplice a' compagni, cioè … … e la partita si giuocherà».
[D] Torino 1787, p. 66: «dovrà andare irremissibilmente, o pagar l'Onoranza doppia … a guadagnar la partita col marcio»; a bid binds (bidding.bid_binds).

[D] Torino 1787, p. 73: «costui pagherà la partita semplice a tutti … giuocare, o far cessare il giuoco»; named for Permesso for three, four and five and for Chiamare il Re (and «a qualunque altro giuoco di Tarocchi»). [R] who the offender may be is not said (any player); the table cannot see a knock, so only the rules page tells it.

[D] Torino 1787, pp. 33-34 (general rule 35): «sarà obbligato senza remissione a pagare a tutti i compagni la partita semplice»; p. 38 (said for Sedici; p. 79 (Meno) and p. 90 (Partita) send to it): «incorrere nella pena accennata … num. 35. di … tutti i giuocatori compagni»; the engine refuses a card that does not follow suit.
